title: cicd-rollback-breadcrumbs-notes
body:
Quick breadcrumbs from the canary rollback incident (notes to self).

Summary:
- Canary deployment for platform-service v1.12.3 (canary=5%) started 2026-02-15 09:10 PST.
- Within ~12 minutes observed increased 500s on /generate and timeouts from downstream embedder.
- Rolled back to v1.12.2 canary -> full rollback to v1.12.1-stable later.

What I saw:
- Error spikes on canary pods (pod-xyz-9f3a2b7): java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space (OOM) in logs at 09:18.
- Sidecar xray logs: high latency to model-gateway (connect timeout).
- k8s events reported frequent restarts (OOMKilled) for canary replicas.

Commands & outputs tried (chronological):
1) kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=platform-service -o wide
   -> found new replicaset rs-platform-service-1-9f3a2b7 with 2/5 pods Ready
2) kubectl logs pod/platform-service-9f3a2b7 -n prod --since=30m | grep -i oom
   -> many OOM traces and GC pauses ~200s
3) kubectl describe pod platform-service-9f3a2b7 -n prod
   -> status: OOMKilled, last state: terminated, exit code 137
4) curl -sS -I https://platform.internal/probe/health | head -n 1
   -> 200 OK from stable hosts, 503 timeouts hitting canary LB IP
5) kubectl rollout undo deployment/platform-service -n prod --to-revision=123
   -> started revision rollback to 1.12.2 (rollback applied to deployment)
6) helm history platform-service -n prod
   -> shows v1.12.3 chart deployed at 09:08, previous v1.12.2 at 08:55
7) kubectl set image deployment/platform-service platform-service=ghcr.io/redwood/platform:1.12.2 -n prod
   -> updated, waiting for new pods to become ready; observed readiness probes failing initially
8) kubectl rollout status deployment/platform-service -n prod --watch
   -> stable back to 100% pods ready by 09:45
9) curl -sS -X POST "https://deployments.redwood/internal/mark-failure" -d '{"deploy":"1.12.3","reason":"OOM during canary"}'
   -> internal marker event created ENG-1427

Hypotheses and notes:
- v1.12.3 introduced a change in the JVM flags (-Xmx bumped to 4g -> actually lower in container limit) and a new dependency that increased native memory (possible leak in JNI extension).
- Docker image for 1.12.3 was built on a different base (openjdk:17-slim -> openjdk:17-buster) — check differences in libc and glibc versions.
- Build pipeline may have omitted the native lib pruning step -> larger binary and memory pressure.
- Canary traffic profile: we route 5% of traffic, but these requests are heavier (longer sequences) and hit model-gateway which had a transient capacity dip — combined effect pushed memory over limit.

Immediate postmortem steps to do (todo list):
- [ ] Reproduce locally: run container image ghcr.io/redwood/platform:1.12.3 with the same resource limits (cpu/memory) and run our long-sequence e2e to stress.
- [ ] Compare Dockerfile layers between 1.12.2 and 1.12.3 (diff and size breakdown).
- [ ] Check CI build logs for 1.12.3 for warnings: mvn native compile steps, dependency tree (mvn dependency:tree).
- [ ] Add a canary health gate for OOM/rate of 5xx within 15 minutes (automated rollback threshold).
- [ ] Coordinate with infra to temporarily increase memory for model-gateway in prod to see if OOM frequency decreases.
- [ ] Run heap dump on failing pod next time (jmap) and collect native memory maps (pmap) — need support from SRE on core collection.

Artifacts / evidence to attach to incident ticket ENG-1427:
- Pod logs: pod-platform-service-9f3a2b7-logs.tar.gz (saved /tmp)
- helm history output (copied above)
- image manifest for ghcr.io/redwood/platform:1.12.3 (sha:sha256:9f3a2b7...)
- CI build link: https://ci.redwood-inference/builds/39812

Notes on rollback strategy (lessons):
- Rolling back by helm revision (helm rollback) is faster for chart values, but image tag set via kubectl set image is more explicit for emergency undo.
- For canary-level failures, prefer automated partial rollback (reduce canary percent to 0) vs full rollout undo to minimize blast radius. Need automation to detect OOMKilled events across pods and trigger canary percentage to 0.
- Ensure image immutability: create immutable tags (sha) in release pipeline and annotate releases with commit sha. I saw a tag reused for hotfix which caused confusion.

Commands to run next / checklist before next deploy:
- docker pull ghcr.io/redwood/platform:1.12.3 && docker inspect ghcr.io/redwood/platform:1.12.3 | jq '.Size, .Config.Env'
- skaffold/local reproduce command: ./scripts/local-run.sh --image ghcr.io/redwood/platform:1.12.3 --mem 3g --cpu 2
- run load test against canary routing locally: artillery quick --count 50 -n 1000 https://local-gateway/proxy/generate

Personal notes: record timeline in ENG-1427, add raw log snippets and grep commands used. Follow up with Aisha on JVM flag changes and Diego on build base image differences. Keep this doc as scratchpad for postmortem draft.

End of breadcrumbs.
